pr.title: Show a pull request's draft state in a color every terminal draws
pr.head: 648f5eb25033f900c38e392aba8973d7739fccd6

summary: Projector's panel is the list above the Claude Code prompt that shows one line for each open pull request the session fixes or reviews. Each line starts with the pull request's number, and a word after it can say where review stands. A click on the header's count collapses the lines into one line of numbers, such as + #12 #14.

Before this change, the panel marked a draft by dimming its number with dimColor. Some terminals draw dimColor at full strength, so there a draft looked the same as a ready pull request. The word after the number appeared only when a review had set a label, and on the collapsed line drafts, reviews in progress, and ready pull requests were all yellow.

Now the number of a draft is drawn in the theme's subtle color, and every loaded line says its state. On the collapsed line, each number takes a color that says what the line's number and word would have said together.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first Projector review of this head found the code and tests sound and opened two documentation threads, both on docs/plugins.md: the example rows above the new text still show a row with no state word, and one rewrapped line runs to 102 characters.
  • A suggestion asks that ready be described as having no review label, not as waiting for a first review, since a push that removes clean also leaves a ready pull request at ready.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Draft. GitHub's draft state, which says the author is still working.
  • reviewing and clean. Labels Projector's review sets: reviewing while a review runs, and clean once a review signs off the current head.
  • Theme keys. subtle, suggestion, claude, warning, success, and error are Claude Code theme colors: muted, light blue, orange, yellow, green, and red.

groups.title: How the panel picks each state's color
groups.kicker: The row's number and word, and the collapsed line's colors, in the hooks module
intro: The panel lives in hooks/register.tsx, the Claude Code hooks module Projector ships. Three small functions decide what a pull request looks like there.

• reviewLabel reads the review labels: reviewing over clean, now in the theme's claude orange so yellow keeps meaning open threads.
  • rowState, new, is the word after a row's number: the review label when there is one, otherwise draft or ready.
  • statusColor is a collapsed number's color, which now checks open threads and draft state before the labels.
The row's number moves from a plain Button label to a Text child of the button, because a Button takes no color and the number needs the subtle color while the pull request is a draft.

files.note: Adds rowState, reorders statusColor, and draws the row's number and state word with them.

checks.text: Each branch of statusColor returns the color docs/plugins.md lists, in the same order; the new collapsed-line test, which passed in the 228-test run, compares every branch's color with a literal.
A draft that carries clean or reviewing shows that label as its word, so on the row only the number's subtle color says it is a draft.
The button keeps its label, which names the control, and draws this Text in its place, as the Button declaration allows for children of strings and Text.

groups.title: Tests that pin each state's color
groups.kicker: One row test and one collapsed-line test, both table-shaped
intro: hooks/panel.test.tsx runs the panel against a fake GitHub answer, with one pull request for each state. The change adds a conflicting draft, #16, to show that being held back outranks being a draft.

files.note: Rewrites the row test to check each row's word, word color, and number color, and adds a test for every collapsed number's color.

checks.text: The row test also asserts the button has no dimColor, so a return to dimming fails it.
